domain: Small CPU-scale machine learning: calibration and robustness of small classifiers on fixed synthetic data
decided: Owner, 2026-10-29: this domain, 4 cases (2 guided, 2 open-ended), 40 turns and 2 restarts per case, about 2 hours per case, Codex

agent.version: recorded in the campaign record at start (provider registry and CLI version)

stopping_rules: Stop when the case's question is answered with verified evidence or shown unanswerable with the given data
Stop at any budget limit; record the attempt as incomplete, never extend the budget
Stop after two consecutive failed protocol runs; record both failures
Never rerun an experiment without a new approval; never edit stored results
rules: The agent works in a new, disposable paper project per case and attempt
Experiments run only as approved protocols (experiment.propose_protocol, experiment.run, experiment.verify)
Held-out data is never given to the agent; only the case verifier evaluates on it
Every attempt is recorded, including null, negative and failed ones; denominators are reported
Every human action is recorded in the intervention ledger (B2)

cases.question: Does label smoothing with epsilon 0.1 lower the expected calibration error (15 equal-width bins) of a logistic regression trained on d1-train, compared with no smoothing, without lowering accuracy by more than 1 point? Use 5 seeds and report paired differences with uncertainty.
cases.method_given: Logistic regression by gradient descent, 200 epochs, learning rate 0.1, 80/20 split of d1-train fixed by seed

cases.question: How does the accuracy of a fixed logistic regression trained on d2-train change when Gaussian feature noise with standard deviation 0, 0.5 and 1.0 is added at test time? Use 5 seeds; report the curve with uncertainty and state any limitation.
cases.method_given: Logistic regression by gradient descent, 200 epochs, learning rate 0.1, 80/20 split of d2-train fixed by seed; noise added to the 20% test part only

cases.question: Find a method that improves the calibration of a small classifier trained on d3-train without lowering held-out accuracy by more than 1 point. Choose, test and justify the method yourself, cite the topic library for prior art, and report what did not work.

Investigate which training-time choice makes a small classifier trained on d4-train most robust to its label noise, as measured on held-out data. Decide the candidates, the experiments and when to stop; report negative results and limitations.
